page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-128GB is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core capability, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth generally fall into the average category. For instance, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are within the middle 50% range. Memory-intensive operations show some limitations, with the PassMark memory score and Geekbench image processing benchmarks performing in the weak (bottom 25%) tier, and single-threaded text processing and bzip3 decompression scoring in the poor (bottom 10%) tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation model offers a more economical entry point for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without needing dedicated, continuous CPU execution. This resource profile is well-suited for memory-intensive but CPU-burstable workloads, such as database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded data processing tasks. It is less suitable for sustained high-performance computing, heavy text processing, or large-scale LLM inference.
